name: 親子丼 (Oyakodon) · Chicken and Egg Rice Bowl
description: "Parent and child" bowl: chicken thigh and onion simmered in dashi, soy and mirin, then set with softly beaten egg and slid over rice. Serves 2.

ingredients.text: 300 g boneless chicken thighs, cut into bite-size pieces
ingredients.item: boneless chicken thighs, cut into bite-size pieces

ingredients.text: a few sprigs mitsuba or 1 scallion, chopped
ingredients.item: a few sprigs mitsuba or 1 scallion, chopped

steps.text: Put 160 ml dashi, 2 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp mirin, 2 tbsp sake and 2 tsp sugar in a small skillet (an oyakodon pan or 20 cm frying pan) and bring to a simmer.

Add 1/2 onion, thinly sliced and simmer 3 minutes, until softened. Add 300 g boneless chicken thighs, cut into bite-size pieces in a single layer and simmer 5 minutes, turning once, until cooked through. Skim any foam.
Lightly beat 4 eggs with chopsticks, just 10 strokes, so streaks of white and yolk remain.

Pour two-thirds of the egg over the chicken in a circle, cover and cook on medium-low for 30 seconds. Pour in the rest, add a few sprigs mitsuba or 1 scallion, chopped, cover and turn off the heat. Leave 30 seconds, until the egg is just set but still glossy.
Divide 450 g hot cooked short-grain rice between deep bowls and slide half of the chicken and egg over each, with its sauce. Serve with shichimi togarashi, to serve.

notes: For individual bowls, cook in two batches with half the sauce each so the egg can be slid neatly onto the rice. The two-stage egg pour gives both set and runny egg, the hallmark of a good oyakodon. Use pasteurized eggs if you're worried about the soft finish.
